statement: Ringwoodite stores 0-3 wt% structural water across the lower transition zone (~525-660 km, ~18-23 GPa).
falsifier: Hydrous ringwoodite inclusions / electrical conductivity show storage capacity outside 0-3 wt% under TZ P-T.

statement: Hydrous ringwoodite descending across the 660 km boundary (rw -> bridgmanite + ferropericlase) sheds water because the lower-mantle assemblage stores far less.
falsifier: Lower-mantle phases shown to retain ~rw-level water, erasing the dehydration contrast at 660.

statement: Mantle water content lowers effective viscosity (hydrolytic weakening), modulating heat delivered to the base of the crust on >10 kyr timescales.
falsifier: Olivine/ringwoodite rheology shows <0.5 decade viscosity drop per wt% water at TZ conditions.

statement: Deep-water boundary state sets a SLOW background sensitivity; it does NOT trigger human-timescale floods directly. Mantle overturn ~1e8-1e9 yr >> narrative window ~1e4-1e5 yr.
falsifier: Demonstrated regional deep-water pulse with surface expression on <1e4 yr timescale.
note: This is the honesty spine. Ringwoodite is the dimmer switch, not the trigger. The trigger is fast forcing on a sensitive base.

statement: Surface water-emergence/flood events cluster where FAST forcings (orbital insolation, glacial unloading, solar, Chandler/annual wobble) constructively align ON TOP OF a high deep-water sensitivity baseline.
falsifier: Adding the deep-water baseline term does NOT improve hit-rate of predicted windows vs fast-forcing-only model above a random-shuffle baseline.
note: The whole model lives or dies here. If the baseline term is inert, drop it and keep the fast-forcing model.

statement: Geographic/temporal clustering of flood & island-subsidence narratives correlates with predicted high-probability windows better than chance.
falsifier: Narrative-cluster dates show no excess overlap with predicted windows beyond a Monte-Carlo shuffle null.
note: Requires a real, dated narrative dataset. Placeholder shipped.

statement: Coseismic / crustal-stress change drives pore-pressure change in saturated aquifers via undrained poroelastic (Skempton) coupling, dp = B * d_sigma_mean.
falsifier: Observed water-level/spring response to known coseismic strain departs from poroelastic prediction with B in 0.4-0.9.

statement: Liquefaction / forced upwelling ('water from the ground') occurs above a seismic-energy-density threshold (~0.1 J/m^3); milder hydrologic response (spring/level) extends to ~1e-3 J/m^3. e(M,r) per Wang 2007.
falsifier: Documented liquefaction at e well below 1e-2 J/m^3, or no liquefaction well above 1 J/m^3 in saturated loose soil.

statement: A primed deep-water baseline (low effective stress / pre-overpressured aquifers) lowers the energy-density threshold for forced emergence, linking the SLOW mantle state to FAST seismic triggering.
falsifier: Sites over high-sensitivity zones show no lower emergence threshold than matched control sites at equal M and r.
note: The bridge between the mantle model and the seismic mechanism.

statement: Emergence narratives in disconnected cultures co-date with regional paleoseismic markers (turbidites, liquefaction features, tsunami deposits) better than chance.
falsifier: Emergence-narrative dates show no excess overlap with paleoseismic-marker dates beyond a shuffle null.
note: Each region triggers LOCALLY. Apparent cross-continental synchrony is a SEPARATE claim (SYN-02): test it against dating resolution and a Poisson clustering null before believing it.

statement: Cross-continental TEMPORAL synchrony of emergence events exceeds what independent regional seismicity produces by chance (i.e. there is a common pacing, not coincidence).
falsifier: Observed cross-region clustering is consistent with independent Poisson seismicity once dating uncertainty is convolved in. Then synchrony is an artifact, drop it.
note: The seductive claim. Most likely to be a dating-resolution illusion. Built to be killed unless the data is overwhelming.
